What is AWS Config used for and how does it differ from CloudTrail?

AWS Config records the configuration of resources over time and evaluates their compliance with rules, for example "do my security groups open SSH to the world?". CloudTrail, for its part, records who called which API. The two complement each other: Config says what changed and whether it is compliant, CloudTrail says who did it. Config is Regional, detects without blocking, and can be aggregated across accounts and Regions.
How do you automate the remediation of a non-compliant resource?

You associate a remediation action with the Config rule: a managed or custom SSM Automation document, possibly calling a Lambda, with an IAM role and retries. Example: AWS-DisableIncomingSSHOnPort22 to close a security group open on port 22. You can also route the non-compliance event via EventBridge to SNS to notify or to Lambda to fix.
What is the difference between an aggregator, a conformance pack and an organizational rule?

An aggregator gives a central read-only view of the rules and resources of several accounts and Regions; the rules are still created in the source accounts. An organizational rule is a Config rule managed centrally across all accounts of an organization. A conformance pack is a bundle of several rules and remediations deployable to one account or to the organization. With Organizations, no individual authorization is needed for the aggregator.
Can you prevent an action with AWS Config?

No: Config is detective. It evaluates after the change and flags NON_COMPLIANT; with remediation it becomes corrective. To prevent, you use SCPs, IAM policies or service guardrails (for example S3 Block Public Access). A good design combines preventive (SCP) and detective/corrective (Config).
Believing Config blocks an action: it has no Deny, it detects and can fix after the fact.
Forgetting that Config is Regional: without aggregation, you only see one Region of one account.
Confusing an aggregator (centralized view) with rule deployment: the rules still have to be created/deployed in each source account (StackSets, conformance packs).
Confusing Config rules with conformance packs: a pack = several rules + remediations; an organizational rule = a single rule.
Neglecting cost: every recorded configuration item and every evaluation is billed, with no free tier.
